summary.tldr: Creates a new kind of restitution order for some offences, letting courts order payment to organizations that provide front-line services to victims.
what_it_does: Adds a new restitution option under the Criminal Code for some offences, letting a court order payment to an organization that gave front-line services to the victim.
Limits that payment to the organization’s reasonable expenses, and only when the amount can be easily shown.

Applies this option to offences of a sexual nature, offences linked to criminal harassment or trafficking in persons, offences involving violence, threatened violence or attempted violence against an intimate partner, and offences linked to controlled substances.
Requires courts to pay restitution owed to a victim first, before any amount ordered to an organization under this new rule.
who_it_affects: Victims of harassment or trafficking offences
summary.background: The bill amends section 738 of the Criminal Code, which deals with restitution orders. It adds a new paragraph that allows payment to certain organizations that provide front-line services to victims.
